title: Outcomes-Focused Sales & CS Playset: Battlecard + FAQ + Demo Runbook
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: Create a compact, outcomes-driven enablement bundle for Sales and Customer Success focused on the March GA. Deliverables: a one-page battlecard emphasizing value props and objection handlers, a contextual FAQ keyed to release notes, concise talk-tracks mapped to buyer personas, and a time-boxed demo runbook that highlights performance, cost controls, and reliability fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: One-page battlecard (PDF + Slack-friendly snippet) that summarizes key messages, pricing sensitivities, and 'ask' for customer next step
FAQ doc with at least 20 Q&A items tied to release notes and known limitations
Three persona-specific talk-track snippets (startup/PLG, enterprise platform, regulated financial) each < 120 words
Demo runbook (6-8 minute core flow) with explicit trigger points for failure-mode fallbacks and a short 'what to show' checklist
Shared folder with assets (slides, one-pager, FAQ, script) and a recorded 20-minute internal walkthrough
milestones: 2026-03-17: Draft battlecard & talk-tracks ready for review
2026-03-24: Recorded internal walkthrough and SE rehearsal
2026-03-30: Final assets uploaded to enablement hub
notes: Focus messaging on predictable latency and cost levers rather than raw model accuracy comparisons to avoid competitive arms race
Include explicit objection handlers for 'we host our own models' and 'we can't tolerate fallbacks'
Design to make the battlecard consumable inside Slack and Sales CRM (1:1 message snippets)
Coordinate with ENG on a short release-notes summary (3 bullets) that ties to customer-facing FAQ entries
rollout_steps: 1) PM publishes draft to enablement workspace and pings Sales & CS leads for asynchronous feedback
2) Run a 45-minute rehearsal with top 4 SEs (cover demo flow + objection responses)
3) Finalize assets, tag in LMS for Sales onboarding, and schedule office hours the week of GA
4) Post-release: collect three deal-level feedback items in the CRM within two weeks and iterate
battlecards: Core claim: 'Consistent, production-grade inference — predictable latency and unit economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.'
Top three value props: 'Predictable latency SLOs', 'Cost controls via caching/batching/quant profiles', 'Unified API for lift-and-shift between deployment modes'
Pricing sensitivity handler: 'Recommend Dedicated for predictable high-throughput; show cost model doc and quick ROI calc (link)'
Competitive differentiator: 'We provide rollout tooling (canaries, A/B) + transparent token-level cost breakdowns — reduces ops burden for platform teams'
faq_snippets: Q: What changed in this release? A: Added autoscaling policies for Dedicated, a cost-awareness dashboard in Console, and a new lightweight fallback routing policy for capacity shortages.
Q: Will existing integrations break? A: No — API surface is backward-compatible; any opt-in features are behind flags and documented in the release notes.
Q: How do we estimate cost impact of enabling KV prefix caching? A: Use the 'Optimize' quick-start estimator (link) and include a sample calc in the FAQ.
Q: Who to contact for compliance questions? A: Customer Security team (security@redwood.com) and your Solutions Engineer for deployment-specific guidance.
talk_tracks: Startup/PLG lead: 'If you want rapid time-to-value, start with Hosted API and enable prefix caching — you get sub-100ms median latency for chat while keeping token costs predictable.'
Enterprise platform: 'Pin a model version and use Dedicated with autoscaling policies — we provide token-level cost attribution so you can chargeback by team.'
Regulated/Financial buyer: 'We offer Private deployments with KMS/HSM and audit logs; our rollout tooling supports staged canaries to minimize blast radius.'
demo_runbook: Core flow (6 minutes): 1) 30s intro to the workload and success metrics, 2) 90s show of Console latency + cost breakdown for a real request stream, 3) 2m live generation demo highlighting streaming + structured outputs, 4) 90s failure-mode: simulate capacity throttle and show automatic routing to fallback variant, 5) 30s wrap + ask
Rehearsal tips: Keep the model selection screen hidden until asked; surface cost dashboard early to anchor value proposition
Failure-mode script: Trigger quota limit on a dedicated pool (pre-configured demo env) and show SE toggling fallback policy to maintain availability
SE checklist: token budget sample, synthetic workload generator link, saved Console view URL, one-liner for each persona
